input:
In /home/eval/pkgs there are dependency lists deps.txt, deps-big.txt and deps-cycle.txt. Each non-comment line has the form `package: dep1 dep2 ...` (deps are separated by spaces or tabs; there may be extra whitespace around names and the colon). `#` starts a comment that runs to the end of the line, blank lines are ignored, a package may appear on several lines (its deps accumulate), and a name that only ever appears as a dependency is still a package.

Write an executable script /home/eval/pkgs/bin/order (bash; awk/sort/etc. are fine, no python) that takes one such file and prints a build order, one package per line, where every package comes after all of its dependencies. The order must be deterministic: repeatedly emit the smallest package (byte order) whose dependencies have all been emitted. If some packages can never be emitted because of a cycle, print the order for the ones that can, then print `cycle: ` followed by all remaining packages sorted (byte order) and separated by single spaces to stderr, and exit 1; otherwise exit 0.

Then from /home/eval/pkgs run it on each file and save: stdout of deps.txt to build/order.txt, stdout of deps-big.txt to build/big-order.txt, stdout of deps-cycle.txt to build/cycle-order.txt, its stderr to build/cycle.txt and its exit status (just the number) to build/cycle.rc.

transcript.final_response: Created the executable script `/home/eval/pkgs/bin/order` and generated all requested files under `/home/eval/pkgs/build`. The cycle run returned status `1`; `build/cycle.txt` contains `cycle: a b c d g`.
tool_calls: cd /home/eval/pkgs && for f in deps.txt deps-big.txt deps-cycle.txt; do echo ===$f; cat "$f"; done; command -v awk; command -v sort

mkdir -p /home/eval/pkgs/bin /home/eval/pkgs/build
cat > /home/eval/pkgs/bin/order <<'BASH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -u

if (( $# != 1 )); then
    echo "usage: order dependency-file" >&2
    exit 2
fi
input=$1
tmp=$(mktemp -d) || exit 2
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT HUP INT TERM

# Normalize records, accumulating repeated declarations as separate edges.
awk '
{
    sub(/#.*/, "")
    colon = index($0, ":")
    if (!colon) next
    name = substr($0, 1, colon - 1)
    gsub(/^[ \t\r]+|[ \t\r]+$/, "", name)
    if (name == "") next
    print "P\t" name
    rest = substr($0, colon + 1)
    count = split(rest, words, /[ \t\r]+/)
    for (i = 1; i <= count; i++)
        if (words[i] != "") print "E\t" name "\t" words[i]
}' "$input" > "$tmp/records" || exit $?

awk -F '\t' '$1 == "P" { print $2 } $1 == "E" { print $3 }' "$tmp/records" |
    LC_ALL=C sort -u > "$tmp/packages"
awk -F '\t' '$1 == "E" { print $2 "\t" $3 }' "$tmp/records" |
    LC_ALL=C sort -u > "$tmp/edges"

LC_ALL=C awk -F '\t' -v package_file="$tmp/packages" '
FILENAME == package_file {
    package[++n] = $0
    next
}
{
    edge[$1, $2] = 1
}
END {
    emitted_count = 0
    while (1) {
        found = 0
        for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
            p = package[i]
            if (emitted[p]) continue
            ready = 1
            for (j = 1; j <= n; j++) {
                d = package[j]
                if (edge[p, d] && !emitted[d]) {
                    ready = 0
                    break
                }
            }
            if (ready) {
                print p
                emitted[p] = 1
                emitted_count++
                found = 1
                break
            }
        }
        if (!found) break
    }
    if (emitted_count < n) {
        msg = "cycle: "
        first = 1
        for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
            p = package[i]
            if (!emitted[p]) {
                if (!first) msg = msg " "
                msg = msg p
                first = 0
            }
        }
        print msg > "/dev/stderr"
        exit 1
    }
}' "$tmp/packages" "$tmp/edges"
BASH
chmod +x /home/eval/pkgs/bin/order
cd /home/eval/pkgs
./bin/order deps.txt > build/order.txt
./bin/order deps-big.txt > build/big-order.txt
set +e
./bin/order deps-cycle.txt > build/cycle-order.txt 2> build/cycle.txt
rc=$?
set -e
printf '%s\n' "$rc" > build/cycle.rc
printf '%s\n' '--- order'; cat build/order.txt; printf '%s\n' '--- big'; cat build/big-order.txt; printf '%s\n' '--- cycle order'; cat build/cycle-order.txt; printf '%s\n' '--- cycle err'; cat build/cycle.txt; printf '%s\n' '--- rc'; cat build/cycle.rc
cd /home/eval/pkgs && ls -l bin/order build && file bin/order && cat build/cycle.txt build/cycle.rc
